subject: sig_sotos_true.csv
text: The analysis found a perfect match to the Sotos syndrome signature, with an AUC of 1.0 and a Z-score of 125.4. All 500 submitted probes overlapped with the Sotos syndrome signature, giving a Jaccard similarity of 0.07 and 100 % overlap. The result is limited to the study itself and does not imply transferability to other studies. The runner-up was Claes-Jensen syndrome with a Z-score of 31.4. No data were missing or refused.

subject: sig_random.csv
text: A total of five hundred samples were submitted and all were present on the 450K platform, with most also represented on the EPIC arrays. None of the twelve cohorts examined met the required criteria, so no best-of-set match could be made. The highest raw area-under-the-curve score was 1.0 for Williams syndrome, but this did not result in a match. Consequently, the overall verdict is “no match”.

subject: sig_sotos_flipped.csv
text: The analysis found a perfect match to the Sotos syndrome signature, with an area-under-the-curve of 1.0 based on all 500 submitted probes, which are also present on the 450K platform. All of the probes overlap with the known Sotos syndrome signature, but the direction of effect is reversed compared with the original cohort. The result is limited to the study it was derived from and does not imply applicability to other studies. The next-best match was Claes-Jensen syndrome with a Z-score of 31.4. No data were missing or refused.

subject: sig_tiny.csv
text: The analysis identified a perfect match to the Sotos syndrome signature, with an AUC of 1.0 and a Z-score of 26.3, based on all 20 submitted probes. This result is limited to the study in which it was derived and does not imply broader applicability to other studies. The next-best match was Claes-Jensen syndrome, with a Z-score of 10.9. In the specificity check, 100 % of the Sotos syndrome cohort (38 individuals) tested positive, while other cohorts showed much lower positive rates. No data were missing or refused.

subject: sig_low_coverage.csv
text: The analysis was refused because none of the 500 submitted probes were present in any corpus cohort, so nothing could be scored. All 500 probes were missing, giving a 100 % missing rate. Only a tiny fraction of probes were found on the EPIC v1 platform (0.4 %) and none on the 450K platform, while the EPIC v2 platform contained all 500 probes but still did not meet the minimum requirement. The refusal code is “insufficient_probe_coverage”. No matches or scores were reported.

subject: Silver-Russell syndrome
text: The analysis found no evidence of a band at the typical case score for Silver-Russell syndrome. The study used controls from within the same series and the interpretation was made between studies, with a pass-structural confounding gate. A signature was built from 64 probes using data from two studies (GSE104451 and GSE55491), involving 63 cases and 16 training controls, and the signature source is rederived and not published. In the leave-one-study-out assessment, one direction was computed, showing a sensitivity of 5/18 and a specificity of 6/6, while the other direction was not computed. The overall verdict was graded.

subject: Sotos syndrome
text: The analysis gave a strong result for Sotos syndrome. The finding is limited to the single study GSE74432 and should be interpreted only within that study. The test used 7,085 probes and compared 38 cases with 53 training controls from the same series. The confounding gate failed, and the overall verdict is that the finding applies only to this single study.

subject: Kabuki syndrome type 1
text: The analysis found no evidence of a band at the typical case score for Kabuki syndrome type 1. The result was assessed across two studies, with 37 cases and 20 training controls, using a signature built from 278 probes that was rederived and not published. The interpretation scope was between-study, and the overall verdict was graded. Both leave-one-study-out directions were not computed.

subject: Down syndrome
text: The analysis was carried out on a single study of Down syndrome, involving 29 cases and 29 training controls taken from within the same series. A signature was built from 3,753 probes, rederived rather than taken from a published source. The typical-case score was moderate, but the confounding gate failed, so the result is limited to the study itself. No leave-one-out directions were computed. The overall verdict is that the findings apply only within this single study.

subject: Coffin-Siris syndrome

text: Coffin-Siris syndrome has 21 cases in this corpus, from 1 study, and its verdict is single-study. Its classifier uses a signature re-derived here, with 8,053 probes. Its controls were taken from another series, so it detects series membership rather than disease. With one study, no cross-study test is possible. At a typical case score the evidence band is Moderate, within one study only.

subject: Williams syndrome
text: The analysis examined Williams syndrome in a single study (GSE66552) with 20 cases and 15 training controls, using a rederived, unpublished signature based on 9,537 probes. The overall assessment was moderate, but the confounding gate failed, so the result is limited to this study only. No leave-out directions were computed.

subject: CHARGE syndrome
text: The result is listed as “Supporting” for CHARGE syndrome, but the confounding gate failed. The interpretation is limited to the single study GSE97362 and applies only within that study. The signature was built from rederived, unpublished data using 907 probes, with 19 cases and 29 training controls. No leave-one-out directions were computed. This finding is not intended for broader clinical use.

subject: Nicolaides-Baraitser syndrome
text: The analysis gives a supporting result for Nicolaides-Baraitser syndrome, but it is limited to the study itself. The signature was built from 4,911 probes using data from two studies, GSE116992 and GSE125367, with 16 cases and 27 training controls. The approach passed the structural quality check and used cross-series controls. No leave-one-study-out directions were computed, and the overall verdict is graded.

subject: ICF syndrome
text: The analysis gave a moderate score for the typical case. The study was limited to a single study and the result applies only within that study. It involved 15 cases and 10 training controls, using 7,740 probes from one dataset (GSE95040). The signature was successfully built from a rederived, unpublished source, but the confounding gate failed. This assessment pertains to ICF syndrome and is not intended for broader clinical use.

subject: 7q11.23 duplication syndrome
text: The analysis was performed on a moderate-scoring case of 7q11.23 duplication syndrome using data from a single study (GSE66552). The result is limited to the study itself and should not be applied beyond that context. The test used 10 cases and 15 control samples, with a signature built from 1,827 probes. The overall assessment is that the finding is based on one study only.

subject: Weaver syndrome
text: The analysis was aimed at Weaver syndrome but could not be completed because there were too few cases, with only eight affected individuals available. The study used data from the GSE74432 dataset and compared the eight cases to fifty-three training controls. The confounding gate was marked as not-testable, meaning the analysis could not be reliably performed. Consequently, no signature was built and no interpretation scope was assigned.

subject: Claes-Jensen syndrome
text: The analysis was for Claes-Jensen syndrome and used data from one study (GSE108423). It included six cases and twelve control samples from within the same series. No genetic signature was built and no probes were used. Because there were only a few cases, the result was deemed “too-few-cases”. The test could not be evaluated further.
